title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on Teichmüller groupoids (Lego construction, cf. Esquisse §3). The previous page treats stable curves X of combinatorial type G with modular dimension 0. These are maximally degenerate curves, with every component a P^1 carrying 3 special points. Such an X is determined up to unique isomorphism by G, because a 3-pointed P^1 is rigid. Grothendieck now builds an explicit, canonical real-analytic model of the 'pair of pants' attached to each component, so that the boundary circles come with canonical identifications for gluing.

Step 1. On P^1 with marked points 0, 1, ∞, let G_3 ≅ S_3 be the group of holomorphic automorphisms permuting {0, 1, ∞}. There is a unique round (positive-curvature, hermitian) metric of fixed normalisation invariant under G_3. Modern reason: round metrics of given area correspond to points of PSL2(C)/SO(3) = H^3. The dihedral S_3 acts on H^3 with a single fixed point, because its rotation axes span R^3.

Step 2. In this metric:
- The real line RP^1 is an invariant great circle (the 'equator').
- 0, 1, ∞ form an inscribed equilateral triangle on it.
- The order-3 rotations fix the poles e^{±iπ/3}.
- The transposition z ↦ 1−z is the rotation by π about the axis through ∞ and 1/2.

Step 3. Choose a G_3-stable system of disks D_i, i ∈ {0, 1, ∞}, bounded by metric circles centred at i. Equivalently, choose one circle centred at ∞ that is invariant under the transposition of 0 and 1. Grothendieck's marginal note says 'c'est automatique', which is right: that transposition is an isometry fixing ∞. The circle must be small enough that its three G_3-transforms (modulo the stabiliser) bound mutually disjoint disks.

Step 4. Normalised model: Σ_I is the oriented unit sphere with a fixed great circle, and I is an equilateral triangle inscribed in that circle. The circles are parametrised by a chordal ('rectilinear') radius 0 < ρ ≤ 1. The vertices are at chordal distance √3, i.e. 120° apart. A circle of chordal radius ρ has angular radius θ with ρ = 2 sin(θ/2), and disjointness requires θ ≤ 60°, i.e. ρ ≤ 1. At ρ = 1 the three circles are pairwise tangent at the midpoints of the arcs.

Step 5. Each Γ_{i,ρ} meets the equator in two points. The next page completes this: each point is labelled by the nearest element of I∖{i}, and the two points are antipodal on Γ_i. Hence Γ_i ≅ U ∧_{±1} (I∖{i}): the circle is the U(1)-torsor induced from the {±1}-torsor I∖{i}.

Step 6. The curve X_G (and its smooth deformations, via a surgery or plumbing model) is then obtained by gluing copies of Σ along the involution of the graph. The tangent circles at double points are canonically U-torsors; for a loop the torsor is canonically trivial.

Purpose: a canonical topological or real-analytic 'Lego' model of a pants decomposition. Each pair of pants carries seams (the real locus, which cuts it into two hexagons) and canonically parametrised boundary circles, up to the ±1 ambiguity. This is what is needed to define the Teichmüller groupoid with base points at maximally degenerate curves.
errors: No mathematical errors. The uniqueness of the S_3-invariant round metric holds only up to scaling; it is fixed by the radius-1 normalisation. The bound ρ ≤ 1 is exactly right: ρ = 1 is the tangency case, so ρ < 1 would be needed for strictly disjoint closed disks, and ρ = 1 gives disjoint open disks.
The phrase about 'ses trois transformés par G_3' with 'le ss-groupe de stabilité' is garbled in the transcription. The intended meaning is the transforms modulo the stabiliser.

ideas.what: Unique S_3-invariant round metric on the thrice-marked P^1, in which 0, 1, ∞ form an equilateral triangle on a great circle (the real line).
ideas.modern_name: Fixed point of a finite subgroup of PSL2(C) in H^3; dihedral symmetric model of P^1 minus {0, 1, ∞}

ideas.what: G_3-stable system of metric disks around the three marked points, parametrised by chordal radius 0 < ρ ≤ 1, giving a canonical pair of pants.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical pair of pants / standard Lego piece; plumbing coordinates at a maximally degenerate stable curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hatcher–Thurston; Ihara–Nakamura (1997) for analytic plumbing at maximally degenerate curves; Bakalov–Kirillov (Lego–Teichmüller game)
ideas.where_published: The Lego philosophy is in Esquisse d'un programme §3, but this explicit metric model is not there.

ideas.what: Each boundary circle meets the real locus (the seams) in two antipodal points labelled by the two other marked points, so the circle is canonically U ∧_{±1} (I∖{i}).
ideas.modern_name: Boundary circle as a U(1)-torsor induced from a ±1-torsor; seams of the pants (hexagon decomposition); tangential base points up to sign
ideas.usually_credited_to: Seams: Fenchel–Nielsen / Thurston school. Tangential base points: Deligne (1989).

missed.claim: Grothendieck works with a spherical (positive-curvature) S_3-symmetric model rather than the hyperbolic one. The boundary parametrisations of the pants are canonical up to an explicit ±1-torsor given by the two other marked points. This builds into the Lego gluing an intrinsic account of the half-twist / orientation ambiguity, which later treatments (Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Bakalov–Kirillov) handle by choosing marked points on boundaries.
missed.quote: le choix des cercles dépend d'un paramètre 0<ρ≤1 (en rayons rectilignes). Pour tout i∈I, le cercle Γ_{iρ} admet deux pts marqués sur l'équateur
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a minor but clean canonical normalisation for combinatorial models of the Teichmüller groupoid. The {±1}-torsor formulation could streamline the bookkeeping of the 'free/oriented' gluing data in the Lego–Teichmüller game. It is not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful canonical construction of pairs of pants with seams and torsor-parametrised boundaries. It is in the spirit of known pants-decomposition and plumbing constructions; only the spherical symmetric normalisation and the torsor phrasing are distinctive.
transcription_corrections: 'petit pour que ses trois transformés par G_3 soit le ss-groupe de stabilité, disjoints des disques mutuellement disjoints' should read roughly 'petit pour que ses trois transformés par G_3 (mod le sous-groupe de stabilité) définissent des disques mutuellement disjoints'. 'disjoints' is crossed out and replaced by 'définissent'.
The model is 'modèle riemannien de la sphère (orientée, [de courbure] 1)'. The '−1' in the transcription is likely a misreading of a crossed-out curvature indication.
'(en rayons rectilignes)' means chordal radii; ρ = 1 corresponds to pairwise tangent circles.
Margin note '*c'est automatique' refers to the invariance of the circle under the transposition of the two other points.
